cls: Antihistamine - piperazine derivative (H1 antagonist) with antimuscarinic/antiemetic activity
pharm: Antiemetic / antivertigo antihistamine (also used as appetite stimulant)
quick: Nausea/vertigo: 25-50 mg up to 2-3 times daily; appetite stimulant (where marketed): 25 mg once or twice daily
May be taken with or without food
Avoid in early pregnancy - piperazine antihistamines historically flagged; use only if clearly needed
Caution - antihistamines may pass into milk and cause infant irritability/drowsiness
Avoid - additive sedation and CNS depression
Sedation; anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention); efficacy
summary: Buclizine is a piperazine-derivative H1-antihistamine with antiemetic, antivertigo, and anticholinergic properties, used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness (including motion sickness and vestibular disorders) and, in some countries, as an appetite stimulant in children and adults. NOTE: buclizine is NOT FDA-approved in the United States; it is available in parts of Europe, Asia, and Latin America - prescribing follows local SmPC/BNF and product information.
indications: Prevention and treatment of nausea and vomiting
Vertigo and dizziness associated with vestibular disorders
Appetite stimulation (where licensed, often combined with multivitamins)

dosage.d: 25 mg before travel, repeat after 4-6 hours if needed

admin: Take orally; for motion sickness, take about 30 minutes before travel
May cause drowsiness - avoid driving or operating machinery until response is known
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
moa: Buclizine is a piperazine H1-receptor antihistamine. By blocking central H1 (and muscarinic cholinergic) receptors - including in the vestibular nuclei and the chemoreceptor trigger zone/vomiting center - it suppresses nausea, vomiting, and vertigo. Its appetite-stimulant effect is attributed to central antiserotonergic/antihistaminic action increasing hunger.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to buclizine or other piperazine antihistamines
relative: Prostatic hypertrophy / bladder neck obstruction / urinary retention
monitor: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision)

preg: Avoid, particularly in early pregnancy. Piperazine-class antihistamines have historically been flagged for theoretical teratogenic concern; use only if clearly needed and the benefit outweighs the risk.
lact: Use with caution. Antihistamines may be excreted in breast milk and could cause irritability or drowsiness in the infant, and may reduce milk supply.
renal: Limited data; use with caution and consider dose reduction in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: Metabolized in the liver; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

moderate: CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines, sedatives) - additive sedation
MAO inhibitors (intensify and prolong anticholinergic effects)
minor: May mask ototoxicity warning signs of aminoglycosides (vertigo)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive sedation and CNS depression
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress skin reactions to allergy (prick) testing - discontinue before testing

serious: Anticholinergic toxicity (confusion, urinary retention, tachycardia) - especially elderly
Paradoxical CNS stimulation in children (excitation, insomnia)
emergency: Severe anticholinergic syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, hallucinations, arrhythmia)

monitoring: Degree of sedation and effect on driving/alertness
Anticholinergic effects, particularly in the elderly
Therapeutic response (control of nausea/vertigo or appetite)
counsel: This medicine may make you drowsy - do not drive or use machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
For travel sickness, take about 30 minutes before the journey
It can cause dry mouth and blurred vision; report difficulty passing urine
Keep out of reach of children - overdose can be dangerous in children
pk: Plasma effect within a few hours of an oral dose
Long-acting antihistamine; effect persists several hours (often dosed 2-3 times daily)
Approximately 4-6 hours or more per dose
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture; keep out of reach of children
pearls: NOT FDA-approved in the US - marketed elsewhere (e.g., as Longifene/Buclifen and in appetite-stimulant vitamin combinations); follow local SmPC/BNF
Piperazine antihistamine related to cyclizine/meclizine - useful for vertigo, motion sickness, and nausea
Also used as an appetite stimulant, frequently in pediatric multivitamin combination syrups (use cautiously)
Marked sedative and anticholinergic effects - caution in the elderly and avoid in glaucoma/urinary retention
Discontinue before allergy skin testing as it suppresses reactions
missed: If used on a regular schedule, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. If used only as needed (e.g., motion sickness), take only when required - do not double doses.
overdose: Overdose causes anticholinergic and CNS effects: sedation or, in children, paradoxical excitation, hallucinations, dilated pupils, dry flushed skin, urinary retention, tachycardia, hyperthermia, seizures, and possibly coma. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive (airway, seizure control, cooling, cardiac monitoring); activated charcoal if early. Children are particularly susceptible.
